message.content:
The number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large – on the order of **10⁴³ to 10⁴⁶**.

A commonly cited estimate is the *Shannon number*, which gives a lower bound of roughly \(10^{43}\) legal positions. More recent computational studies suggest the true count is closer to \(10^{46}\). This figure includes all possible arrangements of the 32 pieces (including promotions), castling rights, en‑passant possibilities, and the side to move, while respecting all chess rules (e.g., no king in check unless it’s a legal capture, etc.).

So, while the exact number is still a subject of research, you can safely say there are on the order of **hundreds of billions of billions of billions** of possible chess positions.
